diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\tilde u_h$ is continuous across all faces of $\partial\Lambda_h$ except those on $\Gamma_j$, the mesh-skeleton contributions cancel pairwise and we obtain

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the cellwise identity (eq:cellwise_entropy_ibp) over all cells produces boundary terms on all of $\partial\Omega_T=(\Omega\times\{T\})\cup(\Omega\times\{0\})\cup(\partial\Omega\times(0,T))$. The error identities in the proofs (eq:1st_term_reformulated in Theorem thm:shock, and the heuristic identity in Remark rem:motivation) keep only the $t=0$, $t=T$ and jump-interface terms, silently dropping $B=\int_{\partial\Omega\times(0,T)}(\mathbf F(u_{\theta^*})-\mathbf F(\tilde u_h))\sgn(u_{\theta^*}-\tilde u_h)\cdot\mathbf n=\int_{\partial\Omega\times(0,T)}\mathbf f(u_{\theta^*})\sgn(u_{\theta^*})\cdot\mathbf n$, since $\tilde u_h$ vanishes on $\partial\Omega$ ($u$ is compactly supported in $\Omega$). No component of the loss eq:loss_func controls the minimizer's spatial boundary trace: $\mathcal L_{bc}$ penalizes only the initial trace, and any $v$ with $\nabla\cdot\mathbf F(v)=0$ (e.g. a constant) has vanishing entropy and regularization loss but arbitrary boundary trace. Hence $B$ is an uncontrolled $O(1)$ quantity and the $L^1$ error bounds are not established as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Augment the loss with a spatial boundary penalty, e.g. $\mathcal L_{bc}^{\partial}(v)=\|v\|_{L^1(\partial\Omega\times(0,T))}$ (equivalently the boundary flux term), and restate the theorems for the augmented loss; alternatively restrict the network class to functions vanishing on $\partial\Omega$. The constructed competitors $\hat u$ and $\tilde u_h$ already vanish on $\partial\Omega$, so their penalty is $O(h)$-small and every rate ($O(h^{1/2})$, $O(h|\ln h|)$, $O(h^{1/2}|\ln h|)$) follows unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The final $L^1$ error estimates of Theorem thm:shock and of every result reusing the same stability identity (thm:shock_interaction, thm:rarefaction, thm:compound_wave, thm:shock_smooth_initial, thm:main_1d, thm:more_general_case) are unproved as stated: each error identity contains the uncontrolled boundary term $B$. The competitor constructions (lem:loss_cpwl_approx, lem:Lu_shock, lem:Lu_rarefaction, lem:Lu_shock_3d) do not use this identity and are unaffected.
issues.title: Spatial boundary term omitted from the stability/error identity
issues.why_classification: The dropped boundary term is a genuine gap in the central stability identity and the stated loss does not control it; however the repair is contained (one additional penalty term, or a boundary constraint already satisfied by the competitors) and preserves the proof architecture and all rates, so the issue is more than minor but short of serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the local DPwP constructions satisfy uniform $W_h^{1,\infty}$ bounds and agree with the same smooth trace data on the boundaries of the $\mathcal U_q$'s, after enlarging the constant $c$ in the definition of $V_h^c$ once and for all we obtain a globally well-defined function $\tilde u_h\in V_h^c$.

issues.failure_explanation: Every error proof inserts a DPwP test function $k_h=\tilde u_h$ into the minimizer bound $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ent}}(u_{\theta^*};k_h)\le\mathcal L(\theta^*)$, which requires $\tilde u_h\in V_h^c$, i.e. $\|\tilde u_h\|_{W_h^{1,\infty}}\le c$. The constructed functions satisfy $\|\tilde u_h\|_{L^\infty(K)}+h\|\nabla\tilde u_h\|_{L^\infty(K)}\le C$ with $C$ depending on $u$, $T$, $\mathbf f$ and the smooth extensions; the constant $c$ in the loss is fixed, and none of the theorems state the hypothesis $c\ge C$. Only the global proof (thm:main_1d) acknowledges this by 'enlarging the constant $c$ ... once and for all'. Without the hypothesis, $\tilde u_h$ need not belong to $V_h^c$ and the stability input of every error theorem fails.

failure_location.quote: By construction $\tilde u_h\in V_h^c$ and is continuous across all mesh faces except those lying on $\Gamma_j$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $c$ is sufficiently large (depending on $u$, $T$, $\mathbf f$) to each error theorem, equivalently define the loss with $c$ taken large enough as the global proof already does; the bound $\mathcal L(\theta^*)\le\mathcal L(\hat\theta)\\lesssim h|\ln h|$ and all rates are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The admissibility of the test functions needed for $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ent}}(u_{\theta^*};\tilde u_h)\le\mathcal L(\theta^*)$ is not guaranteed by the stated hypotheses, so the error proofs of thm:shock and of all theorems reusing them lack their stability input.
issues.title: Missing hypothesis that the loss constant c admits the DPwP test functions
issues.why_classification: A single missing hypothesis repairs the admissibility; the constructions, rates, and conclusions are untouched, so the repair is local and routine.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: on a compound-wave piece, the local construction as in Theorem~\ref{thm:compound_wave};
For compound waves, which exhibit characteristics of both rarefaction and shock waves, we obtain the worst-case estimate $O(h^{1/2}|\ln h|)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts the rate $O((h|\ln h|)^{1/2})$ but provides no proof. Establishing it requires a CPwL competitor and a DPwP test function with the shock interface shifted by $Mh$, a strip-selection term $|\ln h|/M$ (because the competitor loss is $O(h|\ln h|)$, hence $\int|\nabla\cdot\mathbf F(u_{\theta^*})|\lesssim|\ln h|$), a shift error $Mh$ on the regular compound-wave shock, and an interface analysis at the attachment point where the shock coincides with the slow edge of the rarefaction fan. Balancing $|\ln h|/M$ against $Mh$ forces $M=(h^{-1}|\ln h|)^{1/2}$ and yields $O((h|\ln h|)^{1/2})$. None of this is in the source; the rate is consistent with such an argument but is unproved, and thm:main_1d relies on this local construction for compound-wave pieces.

failure_location.quote: The proof follows the same strategy as a single shock (Theorem~\ref{thm:shock}) and a single rarefaction (Theorem~\ref{thm:rarefaction}), so we omit the details.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the omitted proof: adapt the single-shock shifted-interface argument and the rarefaction fan estimates to the compound wave, estimate the interface term as $|\ln h|/M+Mh+h$, and choose $M=(h^{-1}|\ln h|)^{1/2}$; treat the shock-rarefaction attachment point using the bounds of Assumption assump:piecewise_smooth(ii). The stated rate is consistent with this balancing.
issues.overall_effect: The compound-wave convergence rate is asserted but not established; the main 1D theorem (thm:main_1d) inherits the gap for compound-wave pieces.
issues.title: Theorem thm:compound_wave stated without proof
issues.why_classification: The proof is entirely absent and completing it requires a contained reoptimization ($M=(h^{-1}|\ln h|)^{1/2}$) plus an attachment-point analysis, but no new global proof architecture and no rate loss; the main theorem inherits the gap, so the issue exceeds minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We consider one-dimensional HCL \eqref{eq:scalar-HCL} with non-convex flux $f(u)=\frac{1}{3} u^3$ on $[-1, 1]$ with initial data $u_0(x)= \begin{cases}1, & x<0 \\ -1, & x \geq 0\end{cases}$. As the jump $u_L \to u_R$ straddles the inflection point $u=0$, the entropy solution is a compound wave: a rarefaction attached to a shock.

issues.failure_explanation: For $f(u)=u^3/3$ with $(u_L,u_R)=(1,-1)$, the entropy compound wave consists of a rarefaction over $u\in[1/2,1]$ attached to a shock from $u_1=1/2$ to $u_R=-1$ at speed $s=f'(u_1)=1/4$ (solving $s=u_1^2=(u_1^2-u_1+1)/3$ gives $u_1=1/2$). The shock jump is from $1/2$ to $-1$, not from $1$ to $-0.5$. Although a shock from $1$ to $-0.5$ also has speed $1/4$, it violates the Oleinik entropy condition ($(f(u)-f(-0.5))/(u+0.5)=(4u^2-2u+1)/12\ge1/4$ fails for $u\in(-1/2,1)$, e.g. $u=0$), so the description does not match the entropy solution. The reported numerical errors, computed against a WENO reference solution, are unaffected.

failure_location.quote: The reference solution is computed through the third-order strong stability Runge-Kutta method and fifth-order WENO method on a very fine mesh, which has a shock speed $s=0.25$ and a shock jump from $1$ to $-0.5$ when $t>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sentence to state the shock jump from $1/2$ to $-1$ (with speed $s=1/4$).
issues.overall_effect: The description of the exact solution in the cubic-flux experiment is mathematically incorrect; no theorem, proof, or numerical result depends on this description.
issues.title: Cubic-flux exact solution misdescribed: shock jump endpoints wrong
issues.why_classification: A local factual correction in a numerics paragraph; the correction is forced and no inference, theorem, or guarantee depends on the misstated jump.
